WFWorkflowActionParameters.WFCommentActionText: “The unexamined life is not worth living.” — Socrates
“Life moves pretty fast. If you don’t stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.” — Ferris Bueller’s Day Off (1986 film)

WFItems: 1. Spend the first 15–20 minutes at the beginning of each week to reflect on your progress from the past week and gather insights to improve this week.
2. Define what a "win" looks like for the week ahead with 3–5 big picture goals.
3. Translate each weekly goal into smaller, actionable tasks throughout the week.
4. Keep your plan dynamic and realistic: Add/adjust action items during the week. Reassess priorities midweek if needed.
5. Measure progress, not results: Focus on consistency of action (input) over outcome (output). Score yourself on execution rate: What % of planned tasks have been done?

WFWorkflowActionParameters.WFTextActionText:
(1) Roll over unfinished, important tasks to this week.
(2) Drop or delete anything that no longer matters.

WFItems: Reread weekly review notes from the past 4 weeks

WFWorkflowActionParameters.WFCalendarItemNotes:
🍅
──────────────
• At the end of every year, I like to do two things:
    1. [Conduct a reflection on the prior year.](https://www.sahilbloom.com/annual-review)
    2. [Create a plan for the coming year.](https://www.sahilbloom.com/annual-planning)
• My "Past Year Review + Annual Planning" process naturally shifted from focusing on _what I wanted to accomplish_ (New Year's Resolutions) to emphasizing _how I wanted to be_ (New Year's Intentions).

WFWorkflowActionParameters.WFTextActionText:
The Stop, Stay, Start Audit
──────────────
1. Stop: Things I want to minimize/remove/quit (Never Again), What I want to let go of
2. Stay: Habits and choices worth maintaining, Go all-in, Things I want to maximize/optimize, What I wish I'd done more of
3. Start: What I want to lean into
